newsitem.title: DENMARK: Greenland offers to dispose of nukes - report.
newsitem.headline: Greenland offers to dispose of nukes - report.

text.p: Denmark's north Atlantic territory of Greenland is offering itself as a disposal site for scrapped U.S. and Russian nuclear warheads, a Danish newspaper reported on Saturday.

Jyllands Posten quoted Greenland Prime Minister Lars Emil Johansen as saying that the two powers should deal directly with him on the issue and ignore Denmark, despite its formal control of Greenland's defence and foreign affairs.

"We do not want to be a dumping ground, but we would like to contribute to world peace. Our strategic location meant a lot when the great powers were building up their arms, I believe that it can have equal importance now," the paper quoted Johansen as saying.
Covering 2.1 million square km (810,900 square miles) and mostly covered in ice, Greenland straddles the Arctic circle between Russia and Canada.
Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said that he was surprised at Johansen's reported offer.

"It doesn't match what I have previously heard. I must stress that we have had no notification from the Greenland Home Rule Government. If this is real then I must insist that we be notified," he told Jyllands Posten.
The paper quoted the Rand Institute, a U.S. strategic think tank, as welcoming the proposal, one it has previously suggested itself.
"It is good news for the whole world that the Greenland Home Rule Government is willing to take an initiative," the institute's Richard Speier said.
He suggested the U.S. air force base at Thule, in northern Greenland, as a possible storage site.

The base housed nuclear-armed U.S. bombers under a NATO agreement during the 1960s and Greenlanders are still arguing for more compensation for injury and damage caused by an accident in 1968 which resulted in radioactive contamination of the area.
